items.title: A Colorado business council has 49 ideas to make the state more competitive, and a new income tax and a budget gap stand in the way
items.summary: Faster permits, simpler sales taxes and reworked incentives top the list. Council members say last week's tax vote makes the job harder, and one economist asks who will pay for it.

items.title: A regional health panel is deciding this week whether the U.S., Mexico and Guatemala keep their measles elimination status
items.summary: The closed meeting ends Friday. The Americas have recorded more than 57,000 confirmed measles cases and 81 deaths so far in 2026, and Canada already lost its status a year ago.

items.title: The UK economy grew 0.7% in the third quarter, led by technology services, keeping a December rate rise in play
items.summary: Britain's first estimate for the quarter matched forecasts and beat the spring's pace. Services did nearly all the work, and builders went backwards.

items.title: Indonesia's vice president, Gibran Rakabuming Raka, resigns as lawmakers move to impeach him over his school credentials
items.summary: The son of former President Joko Widodo stepped down two years into a five-year term. President Prabowo Subianto must now nominate two candidates to replace him.

items.title: Wolf Creek Pass could reopen to limited traffic by this weekend as Colorado races to patch flood-damaged U.S. 160
items.summary: Two storms tore up the main highway into Pagosa Springs. State transportation officials are aiming for temporary fixes before winter, with a full bridge rebuild lasting into 2027.

items.title: This year's Antarctic ozone hole was the seventh largest in 48 years of records, but scientists say the layer is still healing
items.summary: A large, stubborn polar vortex let ozone loss run longer than usual over Antarctica. NASA and NOAA, whose Boulder lab helps lead the measurements, still expect recovery by the 2070s.

items.title: Alibaba says Hong Kong's exchange has cleared it to spin off its chip unit T-Head in a separate listing
items.summary: The Chinese tech group wants its semiconductor arm to trade on its own. The plan still needs listing approval and a filing with China's securities regulator.

items.title: Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, more than forecast, and traders now expect the Fed to raise rates in December
items.summary: Food, energy and shelter all cost more in October. The report beat forecasts for a third hot month in a row and drew blunt words from a Federal Reserve bank president.

items.title: Israel's president gives Gadi Eisenkot, not Benjamin Netanyahu, the first chance to form a government
items.summary: Eisenkot won more recommendations than Netanyahu, but his own bloc is well short of a majority. He is calling for a national emergency government, and Netanyahu stays prime minister until a new one is sworn in.

items.title: China's factory-gate prices rose 5.7% in October, the fastest pace in more than four years, while consumer inflation slowed to 0.7%
items.summary: Mining and raw materials are pushing up what Chinese factories charge, but households are seeing little inflation. The split points to strong outside demand and a weak home market.

items.title: Nvidia's board opens an independent investigation after reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a suspected Chinese intelligence asset
items.summary: Nvidia's directors say they have no reason to think company or national security secrets leaked, but they will review the reports anyway. Huang, who told staff he had an affair with the woman at the center of the reports, says he will stay on as CEO.

items.title: Jeffco Public Schools' two tax measures are trailing, and a recount on 5A looks likely as the district plans for cuts
items.summary: Voters in Jefferson County appear to have turned down two property tax measures for Jeffco Public Schools. The teacher pay measure is close enough for a recount, and district leaders say more budget cuts are coming either way.

items.title: FTC orders Delta, Uber, Walmart and six other companies to explain how personal data shapes prices and worker pay
items.summary: The Federal Trade Commission has started a study of whether airlines, ride-share and delivery apps and two big retailers charge different people different prices, or pay different workers different rates, based on personal data. It is a study, not a lawsuit. Responses are due within 45 days of receipt.

items.title: Google says it will honor one shared robots.txt signal for AI training opt-outs, but not until 2027
items.summary: Google announced on October 30 that it plans to support a shared, machine-readable way for websites to say no to AI training. The signal lives in robots.txt and comes from an IETF draft. It is not live yet, and today's controls, including Google-Extended, stay in place.

items.title: Two FTC cases in five days target payment-processing fees and hard-to-cancel contracts for small businesses
items.summary: The Federal Trade Commission filed two actions against payment companies that sell to small businesses. One is a lawsuit against restaurant-software maker Toast that Colorado joined. The other is a settlement with a Washington processor. Both turn on the same question: what a business agrees to when it signs up, and what it costs to leave.

items.title: Airbnb's third-quarter revenue grew 19% to $4.9 billion, and the company added up to $12 billion in buybacks
items.summary: The home-sharing company's bookings and profit grew in the summer quarter, according to its shareholder letter. It also guided to 16% to 18% growth for the fourth quarter and said its own AI trip-planning agent is coming in 2027.

items.title: New Zealand's election is too close to call, with National and Labour level on the party vote
items.summary: Prime Minister Christopher Luxon says his National Party has a path to keep governing, but Labour has not conceded. Hundreds of thousands of special votes still need counting, and the new Opportunity Party is headed into Parliament.

items.title: Lakewood police name Agent Nicholas Graham, 33, as the officer killed in a shootout on an RTD bus
items.summary: A Lakewood police agent died and three others were wounded Thursday evening when a man they approached on an RTD bus opened fire. The suspect was killed when officers shot back, and an outside team is investigating.

items.title: Elon Musk says Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production in Texas by mid-2027 to build more Cybercabs
items.summary: The pickup that Tesla once expected to sell by the hundreds of thousands is being phased out. Musk says the floor space will go to the driverless Cybercab, while sales data point to weak demand.

items.title: A Kenyan court sentenced cult leader Paul Mackenzie to 200 years in prison over the Shakahola starvation deaths
items.summary: The sentence follows Mackenzie's October conviction for 191 murders tied to his Good News International Church. Prosecutors had sought the death penalty, and his lawyer says he will appeal.

items.title: Colorado voters approved Amendment 87, replacing the 4.4% flat income tax with graduated rates starting in 2027
items.summary: Colorado will return to a graduated income tax for the first time since 1986. Rates fall on the first $100,000 of income and rise on income above roughly $500,000.

items.title: U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October, far more than forecast, and unemployment slipped to 4.1%
items.summary: Hiring in October came in well above what economists expected, and earlier months were revised higher. The stronger numbers add to expectations that the Federal Reserve could raise rates in December.

items.title: The $6.3 billion Binance theft is the largest crypto hack on record. How exchange hacks happen, who is behind them, and what holders and businesses can check
items.summary: Each of the last three record-setting crypto thefts has been attributed by the FBI to North Korea. The pattern matters to anyone who keeps coins on an exchange, accepts crypto from customers, or holds it on a company balance sheet.

items.title: Marvell agreed to buy laser maker Lumentum for about $115 billion in stock, betting that AI data centers will move to light
items.summary: The chipmaker is paying 4.5 of its shares for each Lumentum share to own the lasers and optical parts that move data inside AI data centers. Both stocks fell, and the deal is not expected to close until 2028.

items.title: Apple's revenue rose 12% to $114.5 billion last quarter, closing its biggest year ever, with tariff refunds adding to the margin
items.summary: iPhone and Mac drove the September quarter, while iPad and wearables shrank. Apple said refunds of tariffs it had paid added about a point to its gross margin.

items.title: Binance reopened withdrawals after a $6.3 billion theft the FBI blames on North Korea, and customers pulled out $3.6 billion on the first day
items.summary: The exchange says it has bought back 90% of the stolen tokens with its own money. The rest are harder to source, and only some coins and networks were reopened at first.

items.title: It is Election Day in Colorado. Ballots must reach election officials by 7 p.m., and certified results are not due until late November
items.summary: Mail is no longer a safe way to return a ballot. Drop boxes and voter service and polling centers are open until 7 p.m., and the first results posted tonight will be unofficial.

items.title: Small contractors are turning to AI voice assistants to answer leads in minutes, and federal consent rules decide how far they can go
items.summary: Research going back to 2011 shows most businesses answer web inquiries slowly. A new wave of AI voice tools, including one launched this month by a Denver firm that shares ownership with Action Global News, promises a callback within a minute, but federal rules treat those voices as artificial and require the caller's consent.

items.title: Two critical PHP flaws sent governments scrambling to take websites offline. What PHP2Shell is, who is exposed, and what to do if you run a site
items.summary: On October 21 the PHP project shipped fixes for two remote code execution flaws in the language that runs most of the web. Within hours, attack attempts were counted in the millions, government sites in Europe went dark as a precaution, and security agencies told anyone who could not patch to unplug. Here is what happened, in plain terms, and the checklist a small business with a WordPress or other PHP site should work through this week.

items.title: Colorado regulators are hearing Xcel's plan to make data centers pay their own way on the grid. Here is what is in it
items.summary: Xcel proposes minimum bills, long contracts and collateral for new loads of 50 megawatts or more. Consumer and environmental groups say a fast-track option for confidential deals could undercut those protections.

items.title: A Denver judge rejected a last-minute bid to knock Amendment 87, Colorado's graduated income tax measure, off the ballot
items.summary: The challenge argued that signatures gathered by improperly registered petition circulators should be thrown out. The judge ruled the law does not allow that remedy. Ballots are already in voters' hands.

items.title: The U.S. ordered non-emergency staff and families out of Saudi Arabia as an attack on Dammam's airport killed one person
items.summary: Saudi aviation authorities said an attack on King Fahd International Airport killed one person and injured eight. It follows deadly attacks on Riyadh's main airport earlier this month.

items.title: Putin agreed in principle to resume three-way talks on Ukraine after November 10, and freed a jailed American, as strikes hit Kyiv
items.summary: The Kremlin set no date, and earlier rounds this year produced little beyond prisoner exchanges. The same night, Russian strikes killed civilians in Kyiv and near Kharkiv.

items.title: Pope Leo XIV needs no further treatment after surgery for an early lung cancer, his doctors say
items.summary: Final tests confirmed a localized adenocarcinoma, the most common type of lung cancer, and found no spread. His doctors say nothing medical stands in the way of a South America trip next month.

items.title: Screwworm has been found in U.S. wildlife for the first time, and in a beef cow in southern New Mexico
items.summary: The flesh-eating parasite, eradicated from the United States decades ago, has been moving north through Mexico. Officials announced both detections on October 21 and are widening surveillance and fly trapping.

items.title: Nigeria has confirmed its first Ebola case, a traveler from Uganda, as the Bundibugyo outbreak reaches a fifth country
items.summary: The patient, a woman who arrived in Abuja on an international flight from Uganda, is in isolation and 44 contacts are being traced. The outbreak that began in the Democratic Republic of Congo in May has now produced more than 9,600 confirmed cases.

items.title: The FAA has certified Boeing's 737 MAX 10, the largest 737, clearing the way for deliveries of more than 1,500 ordered jets
items.summary: The approval completes certification of all four 737 MAX models. The plane also brings a new angle-of-attack safety system that will become standard across the family.

items.title: eBay is cutting about 9% of its staff in its second round of layoffs this year, and Comcast is reported to be planning cuts of its own
items.summary: eBay's chief executive told employees the company's strategy is working and that it wants to move resources to its fastest-growing areas. Separately, Bloomberg reported that Comcast is preparing a significant number of job cuts.

items.title: United and Southwest both posted record revenue, then cut their profit outlooks because jet fuel is eating the gains
items.summary: Both airlines say travelers are still booking at higher fares. The problem is the cost of flying them: fuel prices well above what the carriers planned for in the summer.

items.title: Tesla's profit fell 43% last quarter as it started building Optimus robots and promised Cybercab sales by year-end
items.summary: Revenue was flat at about $28 billion and spending on research jumped. Tesla said the first production-quality Optimus humanoid robots are coming off a converted line in Fremont, California, and executives said they want Cybercabs in customers' hands before 2027.
